chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Yahya ibn al-Mubarak, from Abdullah ibn Jabala, from Is'haq ibn 'Ammar, from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

I said, 'May I be sacrificed for you! Sometimes there is much hair on the back of my neck, which causes me intense grief.' He said to me, 'O Is'haq! Do you not know that shaving the back of the neck removes the grief?'

key_terms.جُعِلْتُ فِدَاكَ: May I be sacrificed for you (a common phrase of respect to the Imam)

ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual or emotional benefit of shaving the back of the neck according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this narration from al-Kafi, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) links the physical act of shaving the nape (qafa) to the alleviation of deep sorrow (ghamm), reflecting the Shia tradition of viewing grooming as a means of spiritual and emotional purification. This specific practice is often contextualized within the broader Sunnah of the Imams, where attention to physical appearance serves to boost confidence and remove psychological burdens associated with vanity or anxiety. The advice underscores the holistic Islamic approach to well-being, where external care directly influences internal peace.

en.hubeali:
A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Yahya Bin Al Mubarak, from Abdullah Bin Jabala, from Is’haq Bin Ammar, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, said, ‘I said, ‘May I be sacrificed for you<sup>asws</sup>! Sometimes there are a lot of hairs in my back, so it grieves me with an intense grief’. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘O Is’haq! But, do you not know that shaving the back removes the grief?’
en.sarwar: 8. A number of our people have narrated from Sahl ibn Ziyad from Yahya ibn al-Mubarak from ‘Abd Allah ibn Jabalah from Ishaq ibn ‘Ammar who has said the following:

“I once said to abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, ‘I pray to Allah to keep my soul in service for your cause, at times hairs grow at my back and it causes great worries for me.’ He (the Imam) said to me, ‘O Ishaq did you not know that shaving one’s back dispels anxieties?”’
